Read the tables inside a filing's text notes

Source: R/note_tables.R
xbrl_note_tables.Rd

A note in an XBRL filing is a text block, and text blocks often hold the note as escaped HTML – table markup and all. This finds those tables and returns their cells, so a specification the filer never tagged can still be read.

Usage

xbrl_note_tables(x, elementid = NULL)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

elementid

Which note to read. A single element name, several, or NULL (default) for every text block that contains a table.

Value

A tibble in long form, one row per numeric cell: elementid, table (its position in the note), row, label (the row's leading text cell), column, column_label (the header above it, which in an accounting note is the year) and value. A note with no table contributes nothing.

When this is worth doing

Where a company tags its staff costs only as a total, the split into wages, pensions and social security usually still appears in DisclosureOfEmployeeBenefitsExpense. Across a corpus of 4,304 Danish filings, 1,302 report the total alone; 1,065 of those carry the note, and 325 carry it as a table. The same holds for fixed-asset notes.

Whether the markup survives is the filing agent's choice, not the format's: some flatten the table to a run of words before writing it into the instance, and nothing can be recovered from those. About a fifth of filings keep it.

Numbers as accountants write them

Danish notes use . as the thousands separator and , for decimals, wrap negatives in parentheses, and write a dash for nil. All four are read. Anything else returns NA rather than a guess – a cell that cannot be parsed is not a zero, and neither is an empty one: treating blank layout cells as zeros invents columns and shifts every figure to their right.

See also

read_xbrl(). Validate what comes back against a tagged total before using it: a table that does not add up has been misread.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_period(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_report_data(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("filing.xml")
notes <- xbrl_note_tables(x, "DisclosureOfEmployeeBenefitsExpense")

# a specification is only usable if it sums to the figure that was tagged
sum(notes$value[notes$column == 1])
} # }
